notice: Hand-authored observation (including nearest markers), probabilities and one sampling draw. Not captured gameplay, real model inference or an executed command. Refs are illustrative.
observationPolicy: Model inputs are HUD/inventory/scoreboard and own grounded/water/motion feedback; renderer-labelled visible pixels, surfaces and current animation; mixed-sound captions; bounded memories of actual observations/actions. Not RGB/audio recognition. No coordinates, measured ranges, hidden entities, future states, health/deadflags or route/LOS probes are sent to the model. The user-approved controller separately compares distances to currently rendered model centers, only after final visible pixels are confirmed. It exports nearest-visible markers, not distances or positions, for automatic binding. The chosen active enemy and pickup are retained in the capped visible lists; remaining entries use screen coverage. Recognized dying/corpse appearances cannot be enemy targets; downed/recovering or unknown poses remain uncertain. Full owned inventory, ammo pools and the actually held weapon's reach remain in the action question. Pickups/ammo never imply ownership. Plain-looking brush functions are not revealed as interactions. Visible references expire on loss; memory never tracks hidden objects.
controller: Normal play asks ONE action-choice question. The model's full public tactic distribution is sampled once without temperature changes, top-k/p or tactical reweighting; rounding alone is normalized. The original SDK answer and replayable draw remain unchanged. The explicit noul diagnostic still ranks independent tactic ratings. Target and weapon questions/sampling are removed: the controller binds the sampled tactic to the nearest currently visible eligible enemy or pickup, using renderer-side model-center distance, and selects the strongest loaded HUD-owned weapon. Power priority is lightning, rocket launcher, grenade launcher, super nailgun, nailgun, double shotgun, shotgun, axe. This fixed order is not a safety or range optimizer; native splash, underwater discharge, spread, ammo refusal and fallback remain. Switch minimums are respected; a held upgraded gun can use its native one-round fallback. Bindings are recorded separately from the model answer at score time and refreshed at application time. A chosen target is held for that bounded command, never tracked through walls or automatically replaced mid-lease. No valid target at application means rejection, not a new tactic or another draw. Execution uses relative movement, visible-pixel aiming, aim-overlap attack, one jump press or swim input. Engage advances only while the current HUD weapon is the axe; stationary/raw attacks gain no advance. A held weapon sends no switch press; a different choice gets one press and suppresses attack only on that tick. Visible loss/death ends targeted input. Pixel aim and explicit look-up/down return pitch toward level after release, bounded to 180 degrees/second, 30 ticks or 750ms, without yaw/movement/attack. Active looks/new targets preempt cleanup; Stop freezes it; Step adds no frames. Live replies older than 60 game ticks or 1500 wall milliseconds are discarded; three consecutive age-only failures stop Auto, without a substitute tactic or relaxed deadline. Step freezes the world during inference. Performance diagnostics are separate from model inputs. Normal physics, weapons, damage and difficulty remain unchanged.
